newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales policy under scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales policy under scrutiny.

text.p: Cobalt players will listen closely to the Defense National Stockpile Center later this month for any changes in how it sells the strategic metal following legal battles with Minor Metals Inc, dealers said.
Stockpile has called an industry meeting on July 31 in Arlington, Va., to discuss cobalt sales.

The event is shaping up to be a renewed clash between those who want to limit or scrap negotiated bids and those who want the metal sold by sealed bid to foster better market transparency and remove "mystery and any manipulation".
"There is a definite split in the industry as to whether or not a negotiated tender services the industry or hurts the industry," a New York trader said.
Stockpile officials were not available for comment.

A Midwest cobalt consumer added, "We will be watching to see what changes have been brought about as a result of the legal developments that took place over the past month or two, and what will be the strategy in negotiated bids from now on."

Lacking any exchange based trading, Stockpile sealed bid sales are the only transparent forum which gives actual prices paid for metal. In Stockpile's negotiated sales, only a rough estimate of total value and tonnage is given.
Some dealers even suggest there may be other lawsuits against Stockpile if futures sales policy is not clear.

"Stockpile is not out of the woods yet in cobalt. The easiest thing for the DLA (Stockpile) to do would be to treat cobalt like it treats spot tin and sell all by sealed bid," the New York trader said.
Without sealed bid sales, the market would be left with only prices gathered and published by Reuters and trade publications, dealers said.
A second New York trader said lawsuits were filed against Stockpile partly because it was not clear on what basis the awarded metal would be priced.
"There was no benchmark established as to how the bids would be evaluated and therefore it was self-destructive," the second trader said. This would eliminate difficulty in evaluating bids, he added.

Stockpile cobalt sales were suspended in March because of two legal challenges by Minor Metals Inc, the trading company that was unhappy with Stockpile's inclusion of a domestic preference clause in sealed bids and other sales issues.
The provision has now been removed from sealed bids, Stockpile said, but dealers wanted to know if the clause will be kept in negotiated bids.
A draft negotiated bid solicitation will be issued on July 18 for the planned sale of 1.5 million lbs in September. A sealed bid sale of 500,000 lbs is due in August.
"Every time there is a sealed bid, everything is sold and is predicated on price - that would be the cleanest way of avoiding anything," a consumer said.
However, this tells the world what the buyer's stocks are and at what price they were acquired, the consumer added.
A second consumer said:"I would continue to encourage the DLA (Stockpile) to use the negotiated bid process. Anytime you are trying to sell somebody you want dialogue."
Consumers also prefer negotiated bids because they have longer term delivery schedules, consumers said.
((New York Commodity Desk 212-859-1646))
